coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across 7 workflow/durable-execution engines in scope: Luigi, Kedro, Apache Beam, Temporal, Conductor (Orkes), Camunda, Argo Workflows. For each product, sourced: official homepage/docs, pricing pages (where commercial), third-party reviews (G2/Capterra/TrustRadius), funding records (where available), analyst reports (Gartner/Forrester), comparison articles, and practitioner discussions (HN, Medium, Reddit). Deduplication applied across multiple comparison sources; sources tiered per competitive rubric (T0=primary capture/live products; T1=official docs/APIs; T2=analyst+reviews; T3=practitioner essays/listicles). Total ~42 unique sources across 7 products. Notable: Temporal well-funded (Series D $300M), Orkes Series B $60M (Apr 2026), Camunda private $126M raised. Gartner SOAP Magic Quadrant 2025 covers enterprise orchestration landscape. Major comparative angles: code-first (Temporal/Conductor) vs visual BPMN (Camunda), Kubernetes-native (Argo) vs microservices (Temporal/Conductor) vs data pipelines (Luigi/Kedro/Beam). HCI pain point evident across reviews: surface-area bloat, cognitive load, debugging complexity in production. Best reference sources: Temporal G2 (4.8/5, 30+ reviews), Camunda Capterra, Akka 10-best-alternatives, Automation Atlas comparisons, SourceForge side-by-side, Netflix TechBlog (Conductor origin). Small coverage gaps: no Gartner analyst PDFs (paywalled), limited Reddit discussions captured, TrustRadius/PeerSpot for Luigi/Beam/Argo sparse.
